business_scope.primary_industry_name: Programmatic Real-Time Ad Exchange and SSP Platform

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (PRC) as the intermediate holding jurisdiction; mainland China as the WFOE formation jurisdiction
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: mainland China operates a civil-law socialist market economy while Hong Kong SAR retains a separate common-law jurisdiction; the WFOE is governed primarily by PRC civil law and the Hong Kong holding company by Hong Kong common law
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Mainland and Hong Kong Closer Economic Partnership Arrangement (CEPA) and its Investment Agreement

Arrangement between the Government of the Mainland of China and the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income
PRC Foreign Investment Law (2019) and its implementing regulations as the statutory investment protection framework
China-Hong Kong Mutual Legal Assistance in Commercial and Criminal Matters arrangement as applicable to corporate investigation and evidence production

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 revision, effective 1 January 2025); Administrative Measures for Beneficial Ownership Information of Enterprises jointly issued by the People's Bank of China and the State Administration for Market Regulation under PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 [2024], effective 1 November 2024; Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision, effective 1 July 2024); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2020); SAMR Measures for Foreign-Invested Enterprise Registration Administration; Civil Code of the PRC; and the Criminal Law of the PRC as it applies to money laundering, fraud, and false beneficial ownership declarations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Hong Kong intermediate holding company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only - apostille issued by the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region under the Hague Apostille Convention; no consular legalization and no Foreign Affairs Office attestation is added.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Continuing Registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only - apostille issued by the High Court of the HKSAR; this path is exclusive and parallel to consular legalization, which must not be chained to the apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney appointing the WFOE legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Hong Kong intermediate holding company, with certification by its registered company secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only - the executed resolution is submitted to the Hong Kong High Court for an apostille together with the company secretary attestation; no consular legalization is applied.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association of the Hong Kong intermediate holding company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry as filed and registered
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only - apostille issued by the HKSAR High Court Registrar; consular legalization is neither available nor permissible for Apostille Convention territories.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Hong Kong intermediate holding company operating account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong licensed bank under the supervision of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only - the bank letter is notarially signature-certified by a Hong Kong notary public and the notarial certificate is then apostilled by the High Court; no consular legalization or Chinese consulate stamp is added.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency, Register of Directors, Shareholders and UBOs of the Hong Kong intermediate holding company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong registered corporate secretarial or registered agent service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only - the certificate must be issued, notarially certified, and apostilled by the Hong Kong High Court; the use of a consular legalization chain is prohibited.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All executive directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorised signatories of the Hong Kong intermediate company must undergo PBOC-regulated customer due diligence under Order No. 3, including beneficial ownership identification, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth analysis, and adverse media review. Each individual must be screened against the OFAC SDN List, OFAC Non-SDN Consolidated List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, HKSAR sanctions list, PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctions list, EU and UK sanctions lists, and domestic and foreign politically exposed person databases. Screening results must be documented in a written AML/CFT dossier, retained at least five years after the WFOE is wound up or the relationship ceases, and any hit, suspicious transaction, or UBO threshold change must be reported through the PBOC/SAMR beneficial ownership information channel and, where applicable, the China Anti-Money Laundering Monitoring and Analysis Center. Bearer shares, nominee shareholding, or bearer warrants are strictly rejected for the WFOE applicant.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Registration System and the local Market Supervision Administration one-stop online name clearance portal, integrated with the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System for post-registration public disclosure.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the SAMR Enterprise Name Registration Administration Measures, the legal name of the WFOE must be written in simplified Chinese characters. The four-tier mandatory naming composition is: administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry or business scope term reflecting programmatic advertising technology or software, and enterprise organisational form suffix such as limited liability company or limited company. Arabic numerals, Latin letters, and roman characters are generally prohibited inside the trade name except where permitted for high-technology or existing-investor names. The Hong Kong holding company's English name must be transliterated into Mandarin pinyin in the shareholder registration materials, but the Chinese trade name must not be a mere phonetic transliteration if such name would be confused with an existing registered enterprise or well-known trademark. Simplified-traditional character conversion errors and translations that are inconsistent with the Hong Kong certificate of incorporation are grounds for rejection.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended once before expiry by filing an online renewal request on the SAMR portal; if local pilot rules permit, the total reservation should not exceed 60 calendar days. If the name is rejected, the applicant must receive a system-generated refusal code and the statutory ground. Within 15 working days of rejection, the WFOE promoter must file a written administrative reconsideration petition with the Market Supervision Administration at the next higher level or the same-level people's government, attaching the rejection notice, the apostilled Hong Kong corporate documents, a detailed explanation of the four-tier name structure, trademark coexistence evidence, and proof of distinctiveness. If reconsideration is unsuccessful, the applicant may file an administrative lawsuit in the competent people's court under the Administrative Litigation Law, or submit a fresh name application using a different distinctive trade name without waiting for the appeal to conclude.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office, PO-box, or commercial mail-forwarding address is not permissible as the sole registered office for a PRC WFOE engaged in ISIC 7310 programmatic advertising and SSP operations. The Company Law requires a lawfully registered domicile, and SAMR will reject an address that is only a mailbox. The local tax authority will treat a mailbox-only address as non-substantive, which blocks basic taxpayer registration, VAT invoice quota approval, and export or cross-border digital service tax filings. Corporate banks will refuse to open a RMB basic deposit account without a physical-site inspection and a lease agreement in the WFOE's own name. A serviced office or business centre may be accepted if it has a dedicated licensed room, a written lease in the WFOE's name, a physical nameplate, and staff present during business hours; a virtual office provider that merely forwards mail is rejected for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: verify the original lease certificate and real-property ownership certificate; confirm a physical office signboard, workstations, communication infrastructure, and staff presence; verify utility, internet, and property management invoices matching the registered address; pay lease stamp duty and retain the stamped lease; maintain a Chinese-language employment and social insurance file; prepare a site-map file for SAMR registration-site verification; coordinate with the tax authority for the new-enterprise site visit during foundational tax registration; and cooperate with bank on-site verification before account opening. Quantified risk: approximately 35-45 percent probability of a physical inspection by SAMR or the local tax authority within the first 12 months for a service-intensive WFOE; the risk rises to 70-85 percent if the registered address falls within a known virtual-office cluster, if the WFOE requests a high VAT invoice quota, or if transfer-pricing indicators are triggered by cross-border digital advertising revenue. A conventional physical office in a Grade-A or Grade-B commercial building with full employment and financial records reduces the inspection probability to approximately 15-20 percent.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SAMR name clearance and WFOE name reservation filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (local Market Supervision Administration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official government fee is charged for the electronic name clearance or name reservation; professional filing support is quoted separately.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Issuance of the Foreign-Invested Enterprise Business License and registration certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory SAMR fee is charged for the business license; the fee was abolished under the current State Council fee-reduction regime.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hong Kong apostille of Companies Registry certificates, board resolution, and articles
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Hong Kong High Court Registry and authorised Hong Kong notary public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hong Kong High Court Fees Regulation fixed government fee plus prevailing notarial service tariff.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified simplified Chinese translation and localization of Hong Kong corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed mainland China translation agency with sworn translation capacity
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per document page plus notarization of the translator's signature where required.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company chop engraving and Public Security Bureau record-filing for company seal, contract seal, finance seal, and legal representative seal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed seal-engraving vendor approved by the local Public Security Bureau
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per official seal set, varying by city and engraving material.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office lease deposit and first-month rent for a physical Grade-A or Grade-B commercial office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial landlord in a tier-1 or tier-2 mainland Chinese city
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rental benchmark per square metre for a small office unit; no government tariff.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Lease stamp duty and office administration charges
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Local tax authority and commercial property management company
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory stamp duty rate of 0.1 percent of total rental value plus property management fee.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO beneficial ownership information report preparation and filing to PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 BENO channel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: PRC corporate service provider or licensed accountant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed compliance service fee for beneficial ownership information collection, verification, and electronic filing.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC, UN, and domestic sanctions screening of directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML database provider and PRC counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-entity global screening package covering PEP, OFAC SDN, UN consolidated, and PRC domestic sanctions lists.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PRC counsel legal opinion on WFOE incorporation, name clearance, corporate governance, and bank onboarding readiness
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: PRC law firm engaged for the formation project
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed legal fee based on prevailing market benchmark for a standard WFOE pre-incorporation package; not a government tariff.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), in particular Articles 4, 8, 9, 23-38, 47 and Chapter VI on company registration; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 2, 4, 6, 13, 28, 29, 31 and 32; Regulations on the Administration of Market Subject Registration; Special Administrative Measures (Negative List) for Foreign Investment Access (latest NDRC/MOFCOM edition).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Market Supervision and Administration Bureau (MSA) of the city or district where the WFOE registered office is located, operating under the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Market Entity (Company Establishment Registration) together with the Articles of Association and Foreign Investment Information Report.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a WFOE established in the permitted advertising-services sector. The shareholders must determine the registered capital in the Articles of Association and subscribe it in full. Under Article 47 of the 2023 Company Law, each shareholder must pay its subscribed contribution in full within five years of incorporation unless a shorter pro rata schedule is elected in the Articles. No blocked escrow capital account is imposed for this non-restricted service WFOE, and capital may be contributed in freely convertible currency or RMB through a licensed bank and recorded under the foreign exchange rules applicable to foreign direct investment.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: THE FIRST WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] CO., LTD. The undersigned directors, constituting the full Board of Directors, act by unanimous written consent without a meeting and adopt the following resolutions effective as of ____________, 20____. WHEREAS the Company was lawfully incorporated as a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company under the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and the Foreign Investment Law, and the Directors desire to establish the Company's share capital, banking arrangements, registered office, and statutory officers. NOW, THEREFORE, it is RESOLVED as follows: 1. Capital Subscription and Registered Capital. RESOLVED, that the registered capital of the Company be fixed at the amount stated in the Articles of Association and that each shareholder subscribe for the number of shares set forth in its subscription schedule. RESOLVED FURTHER, that each shareholder shall pay the subscribed contribution in cash or such lawful asset form as permitted by the Articles and by law within the statutory five-year contribution period, and that the Legal Representative and the Chief Financial Officer are authorized and directed to receive, deposit, verify, record, and acknowledge all capital payments and to issue capital contribution certificates in accordance with the Company's share register. 2. Banking and Payment Authorization. RESOLVED, that the Company open one basic deposit account, general settlement accounts, foreign currency accounts, and such other accounts as may be required for its programmatic advertising DSP/SSP business at a licensed bank in China. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Legal Representative, the General Manager, and the Chief Financial Officer, acting singly below such monetary threshold as stated in the Instruction to Banks and jointly above such threshold, be and each is hereby authorized to execute account applications, mandate forms, electronic banking instructions, SWIFT/Wire and ACH instructions, treasury agreements, and all supporting documentation, and to give receipts and discharges for any funds received. 3. Registered Office Adoption. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be and hereby is fixed at the address set forth in the Articles of Association and the company registration application, that all statutory books, seal registers, and corporate records be maintained at that address, and that the Legal Representative be directed to file all address notices and lease records as required by the Market Supervision Administration. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments. RESOLVED, that [NAME] be appointed as the first Legal Representative and Chairman of the Board, [NAME] be appointed as Director and General Manager, and [NAME] be appointed as Supervisor, in each case to serve until removal or replacement by the shareholder. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Legal Representative and the General Manager are jointly and severally authorized to execute tax filings, employment contracts, commercial agreements, foreign exchange filings, applications for permits, and all instruments necessary or convenient for the Company's operations. RESOLVED, that all actions taken prior to the date hereof by the incorporator, shareholder, and officers in connection with the formation of the Company, including without limitation the lease execution, name pre-approval, and filing of the establishment registration, be and hereby are ratified, confirmed, and approved in their entirety. This resolution may be executed in counterparts and shall be effective as a single corporate act as of the date first written above.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Pre-Approval and Foreign Investment Eligibility Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision and Administration Bureau (MSA) online enterprise registration and name self-declaration portal; NDRC and MOFCOM negative list guidance resources for eligibility screening.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foreign investor must first confirm that the proposed programmatic advertising DSP/SSP activity under ISIC 7310 and NAICS 541810 is not listed on the Foreign Investment Negative List. Because the activity is a permitted digital service without media or manufacturing operations, no specific investment approval from NDRC or MOFCOM is required. The formation agent must then log into the MSA name self-declaration system and submit two to five proposed company names in the standard Chinese corporate name format, selecting the limited liability company and wholly foreign-owned enterprise structure. The proposed business scope must be drafted in conformity with the permitted service catalog and must not include prohibited or restricted wording. The name declaration must be completed by the investor or its authorized representative using a valid identity document and power of attorney. Once the MSA system preliminarily clears the name, a name confirmation notice is retained for use in the formal establishment registration.
required_dossiers: Foreign investor identity certificate or corporate registration documents, including certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, and director register extract if applicable
Duly executed power of attorney appointing the local formation agent
Proposed company name confirmation form completed through the MSA online portal
Proposed business scope statement and Foreign Investment Negative List self-declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected because of identical or confusing similarity to an existing name, the agent should immediately select the next reserved name from the previously submitted list and file a new declaration. If the business scope is queried because of negative list concerns, the applicant should remove the contested wording and resubmit with a more narrowly tailored digital advertising services description. Administrative reconsideration is available if the MSA issues a formal refusal despite correction, but in most cases a revised online filing is faster.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization, Legalization, and Submission of Establishment Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision and Administration Bureau (MSA) enterprise registration window or integrated online government service platform for submission, with prior consulate, apostille, notary, or translation confirmation for foreign shareholder documents.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foreign investor must prepare the Articles of Association in Chinese or in a bilingual format and sign them through its authorized representative. All foreign corporate status documents, including certificate of incorporation, incumbency certificate, and board or shareholder approval of the WFOE investment, must be notarized in the jurisdiction of origin and, where the relevant treaty applies, apostilled or legalized through the competent consular or official channel, and accompanied by a certified Chinese translation. For a Hong Kong SAR corporate shareholder, the Companies Registry issued certificate and related extracts should be certified and, where required, apostilled in Hong Kong with a confirmed Chinese translation. The formation agent then submits the Application for Registration of a Market Entity, the Articles of Association, the name confirmation notice, the legalized investor documents, the identity documents of the proposed legal representative and supervisor, the lease title or ownership certificate for the registered office, and the Foreign Investment Information Report. The MSA will conduct a formal review and, if satisfied, issue the Business License bearing the Unified Social Credit Code.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of a Market Entity (Company Establishment Registration)
Articles of Association signed by all shareholders
Company name pre-approval or confirmation notice
Notarized, legalized or apostilled foreign investor corporate documents with certified Chinese translation
Identity certificates for legal representative, executive director, general manager, and supervisor
Registered office lease agreement or property ownership certificate
Foreign Investment Information Report form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MSA issues a correction notice or asks for additional documents, the applicant has the right to supplement the submission within the prescribed period through the online portal or physical filing window. If the matter is suspended because of defective legalization or translation, the investor should re-notarize or re-apostille the offending document and submit the corrected copy with a cover letter. If the application is refused on substantive grounds, the applicant may apply for administrative reconsideration with the superior SAMR authority or initiate an administrative litigation in the competent People's Court, subject to applicable time limits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, Seal, Bank, and Foreign Exchange Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Taxation Administration local tax service office, local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau, Public Security Bureau-authorized seal engraving vendor, and a licensed bank authorized by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) for foreign direct investment registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after receiving the Business License, the newly formed WFOE must complete the tax registration with the local tax service office using its Unified Social Credit Code and relevant financial and investor information. The company must also register with the social insurance and housing fund authorities for payroll and labor compliance, and must arrange for the engraving of the statutory seals, including the company official seal, finance seal, invoice seal, legal representative seal, and contract seal, at a licensed engraving company supervised by the Public Security Bureau. The legal representative or authorized officer must then open a basic deposit bank account and any supplementary settlement or foreign currency accounts with a licensed bank. If the foreign shareholder intends to inject capital from outside mainland China, the WFOE must complete the foreign exchange registration for foreign direct investment through the bank, submit the relevant capital contribution source documents, and retain all capital contribution receipts for later capital verification and tax reporting. All tax, social insurance, employment, and statistical registrations should be completed within the statutory 30-day window from the date of license issuance.
required_dossiers: Business License confirming the Unified Social Credit Code
Tax Registration Application and financial information disclosure forms
Social insurance and housing fund registration information
Seal engraving authorization letter with legal representative identity certificate
Basic deposit account opening application, bank KYC forms, and company authorization matrix
Foreign direct investment foreign exchange registration questionnaire and capital contribution source documents if inbound capital is deployed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or SAFE query identifies incomplete KYC or capital source documentation, the company should promptly provide bank statements, board resolutions, and a source-of-funds letter from the foreign shareholder. If tax registration is filed late, the company should make the filing immediately, include an explanation, and pay any minimal late-filing penalty if assessed. A rejected seal engraving application is cured by correcting the authorization form and resubmitting to the same authority. None of these defects invalidate the underlying incorporation if corrected promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution Ratification and Statutory Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company registered office, board of directors or sole shareholder acting by written consent, the legal representative, and external counsel; local MSA may accept corrective filings if the record is later challenged.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the Business License and bank account are in place, the shareholder and directors must formally convene or act by unanimous written consent to approve the First Board Resolution. The resolution must ratify the subscribed share capital, confirm the responsible officers, adopt the registered office, and authorize banking signatories. The company must prepare and maintain the statutory register of members, register of directors, register of supervisors, transfer ledger, and minute book at the registered office. Share certificates or capital contribution certificates must be issued to each shareholder and entered into the share register. The company seal register should define custody, approval levels, and usage logging requirements. If the actual paid-in capital differs from the initial subscribed capital or if contributions are made in instalments, the company must record those events accurately and file any required paid-in capital modifications or annual reports with the MSA in accordance with law.
required_dossiers: Draft First Board Resolution or sole shareholder written consent
Capital subscription schedule and paid-in capital contribution records
Share certificates or capital contribution certificates
Appointment letters for legal representative, general manager, and supervisor
Company seal usage and authorization matrix
Statutory registers of members, directors, supervisors, and minutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the local MSA or an external auditor later disputes the share capital records or officer appointments, the company may call a further shareholder or board meeting and ratify a supplemental resolution. The corrected minutes and forms should then be filed as a record amendment or change registration with the MSA. Any ambiguity in the banking authorization is cured by issuing a revised Instruction to Banks signed by the same authorized signatories and countersigned by the legal representative.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. The WFOE operates purely as a digital programmatic advertising exchange, DSP and SSP platform classified under ISIC 7310 and NAICS 541810. It does not conduct physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing operations under ISIC 1xxx, 2xxx, 3xxx, 4xxx or 52xx, and therefore no municipal industrial licensing board or manufacturing authority is invoked.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable at the industrial manufacturing level. No physical operating permit, production license, or factory registration is required for this pure digital advertising technology service. Any separate internet information service or online advertising platform filing that might be relevant is not an industrial or physical license and is assessed under a different regulatory track.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable. The Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) and its provincial or municipal environmental protection bureaus would be the competent agencies if a physical project existed, but none exists for a pure software-based programmatic advertising platform.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no EIA Filing, Environmental Registration, or Full EIA Report is required because the project creates no construction works, no production facility, no wastewater discharge, and no industrial stationary emission source.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: None. The digital DSP/SSP activity generates no process wastewater, fuel combustion emissions, volatile organic compounds, hazardous chemical storage, or industrial solid waste. Office-related ordinary solid waste shall be handled through municipal collection services, and any electronic waste shall be disposed through licensed recyclers. No quantitative discharge limit or emissions threshold applies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable to industrial civil-defense fire permits because the company has no manufacturing, chemical, or warehousing premises. The commercial office used as the registered office must nevertheless maintain basic fire safety compliance, such as a valid property fire acceptance certificate or equivalent landlord-provided fire safety documentation, fire extinguishers, emergency exits, and compliance with the Fire Protection Law of the People's Republic of China. No special Civil Defense permit for factory or warehouse operations is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA) via the Electronic Tax Bureau portal at etax.chinatax.gov.cn, and the Inland Revenue Department of the Hong Kong SAR (IRD) via the eTax portal at www.ird.gov.hk for Hong Kong-source profits or filings of any Hong Kong affiliate
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The WFOE is incorporated with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), which issues the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) that serves as the taxpayer identification number for PRC tax purposes. Immediately after incorporation, the WFOE must complete tax registration with the local STA office through the Electronic Tax Bureau, binding the USCC to the tax dossier, electing VAT taxpayer status, and registering for corporate income tax, VAT, stamp duty, and urban maintenance and construction tax. For foreign non-resident parent entities with no permanent establishment in mainland China, any PRC-source income is subject to withholding tax at the statutory rate and requires a withholding agent registration under the same USCC/TIN framework; the non-resident must obtain a certificate of tax residence from its home jurisdiction for treaty relief. In Hong Kong, a non-resident company deriving Hong Kong-source profits is treated by the IRD under the territorial source principle and must obtain a Business Registration Certificate under the Business Registration Ordinance; there is no separate VAT/GST registration in Hong Kong. The WFOE should also ensure any Hong Kong affiliate maintains an active IRD taxpayer file and prepares the offshore profits claim documentation if profits are derived entirely outside Hong Kong.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC tax system does not provide a check-the-box or partnership classification election for WFOEs; a WFOE is always a resident enterprise taxed on worldwide income at the entity level under the Enterprise Income Tax Law. Hong Kong applies the territorial source principle, but no check-the-box election exists; entities may elect to claim offshore profits treatment or foreign tax credit arrangements under the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Ordinance. Hybrid mismatch elections are not available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax) for mainland China; Hong Kong SAR has no VAT or GST system but imposes Business Registration and Profits Tax under the Inland Revenue Ordinance
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 (Renminbi five million) annual taxable sales for mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration in mainland China; foreign entities making taxable supplies in mainland China must register for VAT regardless of turnover threshold, while Hong Kong does not impose VAT/GST registration thresholds
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mainland China mandates electronic invoicing through the national Electronic Invoice Service Platform, with all VAT special invoices and general invoices subject to real-time transmission to the State Taxation Administration, digital stamping, tax-control QR codes, and integration with the WFOE's Unified Social Credit Code. The fully digital electronic invoice regime requires API-based issuance, automatic clearance against registered tax rates, and immediate invoice authenticity verification through the National VAT Invoice Verification Platform. Hong Kong does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance or e-invoice mandate; invoices are governed by the Inland Revenue Ordinance record-keeping requirements and the Business Registration Ordinance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under PRC VAT law, goods exported by the WFOE are zero-rated and eligible for VAT export rebate upon full customs exportation. For programmatic advertising, DSP/SSP, and other cross-border services under ISIC 7310, zero-rating or VAT exemption is available under the cross-border taxable activity rules for services that are supplied to overseas entities and consumed entirely outside mainland China; the WFOE must prove the service is rendered to a non-resident customer, the benefit of the service arises outside mainland China, and consideration is received in foreign exchange. The Hong Kong offshore profits claim follows the territorial source principle, requiring the Hong Kong entity, if any, to substantiate that profits arise from contracts concluded and services performed outside Hong Kong to qualify for non-taxation in Hong Kong.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export customs declaration with customs seal or electronic release), Bill of Lading or equivalent air waybill or master transport document, Foreign Exchange Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC), foreign trade contract, commercial invoice, packing list, and product authenticity proof for goods export; for cross-border digital advertising services, the bundle must include the signed offshore service agreement, delivery and service acceptance evidence, payment confirmation through SWIFT or ACH rails, bank inward remittance certificate, and a declaration of offshore consumption

Cross-border service export substantiation: no physical customs declaration is required, but the taxpayer must retain electronic records showing the recipient's non-resident status and the offshore location of the advertising inventory or SSP/DSP services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The State Taxation Administration and customs authorities may audit export-rebate claims and cross-border zero-rated service filings. Failure to satisfy the documentary, customs-clearance, or foreign-exchange-repatriation conditions triggers disallowance of the zero-rating, forced VAT recapture, clawback of any refunded output tax, and imposition of interest. The PRC Tax Collection Administration Law further authorizes late payment surcharges at 0.05% per day, penalties from 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax, and administrative fines; fraudulent export refund claims can lead to criminal liability for tax evasion. In Hong Kong, incorrect offshore profit claims may result in additional assessments, penalties of up to 300% of the tax understated, and prosecution under the Inland Revenue Ordinance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), operating under the policy direction of the People's Bank of China (PBOC), is the operative central bank and FX administration authority for the mainland-incorporated WFOE; the Hong Kong SAR parent operates under the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) with no currency-control restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Mainland China operates a managed current-account convertibility framework under the Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations (2008) and the PBOC/SAFE implementing circulars. RMB is convertible for bona fide trade in goods and services, including programmatic advertising technology fees, once banks verify underlying contracts, invoices and three-party service relationship. Capital-account items, including inbound equity injections from the Hong Kong parent to the WFOE, require prior FDI registration with SAFE in the Capital Project Information System, followed by establishment of a dedicated foreign-currency capital account at a domestic bank. Profit remittances to the Hong Kong shareholder are treated as current-account dividends and are legally remittable after annual audit, but the bank must review the audited financial statements, China-corporate income tax settlement/payment proof, board dividend resolution, and AML beneficial-ownership confirmation. Surrender or mandatory conversion does not apply uniformly to current-account receipts, but export proceeds must be repatriated and, if held in a settlement account, subject to retention quotas. For capital inflows, the foreign currency must be converted to CNY through the bank at market rate and used within the approved expenditure scope. Therefore, while not a fully convertible jurisdiction, a WFOE can execute repatriation and settlement with rigorous documentary support.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: SAFE requires export foreign-exchange proceeds to be repatriated to the domestic delegated bank's Forex settlement account within the earlier of the trade-maturity date set in the sales contract or the statutory 90-day default from the performance/shipment date; banks are then obligated to credit the exporter and apply verification in the SAFE monitoring system. The foreign-currency settlement account retention quota is computed by the bank based on the exporter's verified current-account receipts from the previous 12 months. Any amount above that approved quota must be sold to the designated bank at the spot market rate, effectively a 100% mandatory surrender of the surplus and conversion into CNY. No fixed proportional surrender applies to the retained quota, but the exporter may voluntarily convert all or part.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (SAFE-registered FDI capital account) and Basic Operational Currency Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational CNY/USD Account and Cross-Border Settlement Account
Basic Operational Account and Foreign Currency Settlement Account
Basic Operational Account and Reserve Foreign Exchange Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Onshore Chinese banking law and PBOC/SAFE licensing require a licensed domestic banking institution with access to CNAPS and the SAFE Capital Project Information System. Offshore digital EMIs such as Airwallex, Revolut, Payoneer, and Currenxie are neither licensed nor regulated as depository institutions in mainland China and cannot hold a WFOE's CNY operating accounts, receive FDI capital-account remittances, perform statutory tax or SAFE reporting, or support a CPA capital-verification report. Their practical utility is confined to ancillary fund flows of the Hong Kong holding entity in non-CNY corridors and they cannot replace domestic bank rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under PBOC Beneficial Ownership Identification Measures and banking KYC directives, the WFOE's statutory legal representative and at least one authorized signatory must appear physically at the domestic branch for the initial corporate account opening and KYC interview. Remote consular proxy opening, where the Hong Kong shareholder signs a notarized power of attorney without any on-site presence, is generally not acceptable for the base KYC account. After the first interview and signature validation, subsequent board or mandate changes may be processed through consular-notarized authorization. A conditional video KYC interview is occasionally allowed only if the bank's approved remote-onboarding framework has been invoked and the UBO identity has been verified through an onshore notary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection source-of-funds opacity: the Hong Kong parent is a recently formed investment holding vehicle without a substantive balance-sheet history, increasing suspicion that the equity injection is undisclosed third-party funding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of HK parent's Certificate of Incorporation and Business Registration Certificate; register of members and share-transfer log; audited financial statements or consulate-notarized management accounts for the prior 18 months; original bank statements of the HK parent account showing accumulated retained earnings; board resolution approving the capital contribution; notarized ultimate beneficial owner declaration signed by every 10% or greater shareholder; and a source-of-wealth statement supported by employment, corporate dividends, liquidation or family trust records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear or high-risk business purpose: programmatic ad exchange, DSP and SSP services can be mischaracterized as online gambling, fraudulent ad arbitrage or unlicensed money-services business because of fragmented high-frequency cross-border payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed commercial agreements with advertisers, DSP partners, publishers and SSP clients; technical integration architecture diagram evidencing real-time bidding, impression tracking and server-side ad serving; sample invoices and billing statements from at least three platform clients; ISAE 3402 / SOC 2 report covering the ad-server control environment; and any applicable ICP record or advertising license obtained from the Chinese telecom and commercial authorities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner tax-residence and domicile mismatch: the ultimate individual owner appears as a tax resident in another jurisdiction while managing the mainland WFOE, creating red flags for personal tax evasion, illegal capital flight or artificial offshore structuring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passport copy plus a certificated tax-residency confirmation (Tax Residency Certificate or equivalent) aligned with the stated residence; China Individual Income Tax filing records or a notarized statement of tax status; employment contract, board minutes and substance documents proving actual management and decision-making in the stated jurisdiction; WFOE board minutes resolving dividend policy and financing; and personal wealth declaration demonstrating lawful acquisition of the HK shares.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume transaction fragmentation: expected large numbers of SWIFT MT103 payments and low-value disbursements may be interpreted as structuring, layering, or concealment of commercial flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A formal treasury projection model including historical transaction volumes, counterparty jurisdictions and settlement-cycle assumptions; written flow diagram of advertiser, DSP, publisher and SSP payments; segregated reconciliation reports by client showing bid-level settlement arithmetic; an enterprise-wide AML compliance program with transaction monitoring and sanctions-screening procedures; and evidence of an appointed AML compliance officer and external audit engagement letter.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Hong Kong parent wires equity consideration through its licensed HK bank using SWIFT MT103/MT202 to the WFOE's dedicated foreign-currency capital account at the selected onshore bank. Prior to remittance, the WFOE must complete SAFE foreign direct investment (FDI) registration and obtain the SAFE Capital Project identification number, which the receiving bank will verify in the Capital Project Information System. The remittance reference field must contain 'WFOE CAPITAL INJECTION - SAFE FDI REGISTRATION NO. [NUMBER]' and match the SAFE transaction purpose code for inbound direct-investment equity contribution. Upon receipt, the onshore bank converts the HKD/USD to CNY only for approved expenditure categories, and a Chinese certified public accountant issues the statutory capital-verification report which is subsequently filed with the local Market Supervision Administration / SAMR. No disbursement from the capital account occurs before KYC review, SAFE matching, and FX-conversion purpose compliance have been fully completed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For domestic operating costs such as payroll, server hosting, tax and local vendor services, the WFOE should use CNY disbursements through CNAPS from its basic deposit account. For cross-border service fees owed to foreign publishers, advertisers, SSP partners or data vendors, SWIFT MT103 is the appropriate clearing rail, supported by the underlying service contract, itemized invoice and SAFE current-account transaction declaration. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are structurally unsuitable for pure digital advertising services where settlement events are data-driven and recurring; standby LCs or bank payment undertakings may be used only where payment certainty is contractually required. Cross-border RMB settlement can be routed via CIPS through the same relationship bank, reducing USD conversion cost and correspondent-bank latency, and every transfer must be tagged with the relevant current-account FX purpose code.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward contracts with genuine underlying current-account or capital-account exposure, concluded with a licensed domestic bank under ISDA/NAFMII documentation and verified by SAFE exposure reviews.
Onshore FX swaps and cross-currency swaps used to hedge real operational, dividend or intercompany loan exposures, subject to SAFE registration and bank-supported risk exposure validation.

Offshore NDFs are generally not permitted for the mainland WFOE; only the Hong Kong parent may access offshore CNH NDF markets, and the onshore entity must limit derivatives to fully deliverable instruments with genuine trade or servicing exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form NAR1) for a private company limited by shares
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary date of incorporation; the annual return date is the company's incorporation anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee scale: HKD 1,260 if over 42 days but not more than 3 months; HKD 2,520 over 3 but not more than 6 months; HKD 3,780 over 6 but not more than 9 months; HKD 5,040 over 9 but not more than 12 months; after 12 months the Registrar may prosecute (fine up to HKD 100,000 plus daily default fine) and administratively strike the company off the register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the expiry date shown on the current Business Registration Certificate; the Inland Revenue Department issues the renewal demand note before expiry and payment is due within one month of the demand note date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of HKD 300; continued non-renewal may result in prosecution with fines up to HKD 10,000 and imprisonment up to 6 months, and the company may be treated as carrying on unregistered business, leading to strike-off action by the Companies Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return (Form BIR51) for corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 1 month from the date of issue of the return; with a tax representative, commonly extended to 15 August for a 31 December year-end and 15 November for a 31 March year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The Inland Revenue Department may issue an estimated assessment; on conviction, a fine up to HKD 10,000 and additional tax up to three times the undercharged tax; unpaid tax may attract 5% additional tax after 6 months and a further 5% after another 6 months.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Presentation of audited annual financial statements and directors' report to members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Members of the company; minutes retained in the statutory minute book (no regulator receipt unless audited financial statements are submitted under another filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 9 months after the end of the financial year for a non-listed company, or within 4 months for a listed company, unless a unanimous member resolution dispenses with the meeting requirement under the Companies Ordinance.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence by the company and every responsible officer; maximum fine at level 3 (HKD 10,000) plus daily default fine for continuing contravention; persistent default may be raised by the Companies Registry as evidence that the company is not carrying on business and supports strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return (Form BIR56A and related IR56B statements) if any employee or director remuneration is paid
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 1 May in each year of assessment, or within one month from the issue date if a different date is specified on the return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing can result in a fine up to HKD 10,000 and further penalty up to three times undercharged tax; the Inland Revenue Department may issue an estimated assessment for employees.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: In Hong Kong there is no general turnover, asset, or headcount exemption for active private limited companies: every active company must appoint an independent certified public accountant (CPA) holding a Practising Certificate to audit its annual financial statements. Quantitative size criteria (HKD 25 million revenue, HKD 25 million assets, 50 employees) are not audit exemptions but are relevant only to classification for simplified financial reporting; a dormant private company that files a dormant status declaration may be exempt while dormant, but any trading or exchange activity in the programmatic ad exchange business triggers an immediate mandatory audit obligation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS), which converge with IFRS; eligible private entities without public accountability may apply HKFRS for Private Entities (the local SME standard). All financial statements must give a true and fair view and comply with the Companies Ordinance (Cap 622) and the Companies (Audit) Regulations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not require a UBO return to be filed annually with the Companies Registry. Instead, the company must maintain a Significant Controllers Register (SCR) at the registered office or a specified place, identifying every significant controller (individual or entity holding 25% or more of shares/voting rights or otherwise controlling the company). The SCR must be updated within 7 days of any relevant change, and law enforcement and authorized officers must be given access. There is no 30-day reporting window for share transfers at the registrar; all share transfers are recorded in the Register of Members and the annual return Form NAR1 confirms the register on the anniversary date, and any allotment/transfer-related changes are captured through separate Companies Registry filings where legally required.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 900 per annum for registered office and company secretary services in Hong Kong
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 12,000 per annum for an active programmatic advertising DSP/SSP entity with cross-border transactions; lower end for a dormant or simple private entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: High and New Technology Enterprise (HNTE) 15% rate; Small Low-Profit Enterprise preferential effective 5% rate on taxable income up to RMB 3 million (subject to current policy sunset); 100% super deduction for qualified R&D expenses; software/adtech enterprise dual-exemption and half-rate incentive if certified; no automatic free-zone holiday in mainland China.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: A100000 (Annual Corporate Income Tax Return, Class A) and related schedules filed through the State Taxation Administration (STA) electronic tax portal (Golden Tax IV); quarterly provisional payments using prepayment forms on same portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual reconciliation plus quarterly provisional prepayments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return: on or before 31 May immediately following the close of the tax year. Quarterly provisional payments: within 15 calendar days after each quarter-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating revenue, including programmatic advertising exchange fees, DSP/SSP platform commissions and ad tech services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognise revenue on a gross commission or principal basis in accordance with contractual facts. Cross-border chain billing from the HK SSP to the WFOE must be evidenced by contracts and platform records; if the WFOE is merely a commissionaire of the HK parent, only commission is revenue, and a permanent establishment (PE) exposure for the HK parent must be analysed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating costs, including media inventory purchases, data/bandwidth costs, licensed ad-serving algorithms and content delivery.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party cost payments to the HK parent or offshore affiliates require arm's length prices and contemporaneous TP documentation. Any royalty component embedded in 'data access' payments must be split out, subject to royalty withholding tax, and capitalised/expensed only if economically beneficial and deductible under PRC CIT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxes and surcharges other than CIT and VAT, e.g. urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, stamp duty.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No non-resident item is included here. VAT collected on outbound digital advertising services may be zero-rated/export VAT-exempt only if the service is rendered to non-resident enterprises outside China; erroneous VAT rebate claims can trigger tax fraud penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling expenses, such as channel commissions, traffic acquisition, marketing and business development costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Commissions paid to HK/offshore media brokers are business profits of the broker; under the HK DTA they are not taxable in China unless attributable to a PE in China. To avoid recharacterisation, the agreement should be for services, not for use of software or intangible rights; service fee withholding at 10% applies only if the fee is China-source service income with PE/tax nexus or is re-categorised as royalty/technical service.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Administrative expenses, including legal, accounting, corporate, rent and general overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees paid to the HK parent are not deductible if they are simple allocations without specific services. Allocated group overhead from the HK parent must be supported by cost-sharing agreements, actual service evidence, and benefit tests; otherwise the amount is added back and an interest/penalty regime applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial expenses, including interest on intercompany loans, bank charges, hedging costs and foreign exchange losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid by the WFOE to the HK parent is China-source income; statutory WHT is 10%, reduced to 7% under the HK DTA upon submission of TRC and beneficial ownership documentation. The deductible amount is capped by China's thin capitalisation rule (debt-to-equity ratio 2:1 generally, 5:1 for financial institutions) and arm's length interest rate; excess disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Asset impairment losses and bad debt provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: General provisions and impairment of advertising technology receivables are non-deductible until actual loss occurs; related-party receivables from HK affiliates require written-off proof and a special filing, otherwise the add-back is mandatory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fair value changes on financial instruments and investment properties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Unrealised fair-value gains/losses from derivatives used to hedge USD ad revenue are generally tax-neutral until realisation; conversion into RMB for tax payment does not create a deductible foreign-exchange loss unless actually realised and designated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Investment income, including dividends, interest and equity-transfer gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends received by the WFOE from a Chinese resident enterprise are tax-exempt. Distributions from a HK subsidiary could be caught by China's Controlled Foreign Corporation rule if the HK entity is low-taxed and fails the economic substance/CIGA business test; proper attribution and CFC exemption analysis should be attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income, such as government subsidies, debt forgiveness and asset disposals.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Government grants for ad-tech or high-tech projects are taxable unless qualifying as capital grants under the State Council's special treatment; non-qualifying subsidies received from HK/offshore sponsors must be included in full.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating expenses, including fines, penalties, donations and asset-scrapping losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax penalties, administrative fines, and illegal payments are non-deductible; charitable donations are deductible only through approved social organisations and within 12% of annual accounting profit; payments to non-resident entities not properly documented are disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total accounting profit before income tax, as reconciled to the statutory financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This figure must match the audited PRC GAAP income statement. The HK parent's consolidation or group reporting should not alter the legal entity accounts of the WFOE; equity method income from non-resident investees may require tax adjustment in later boxes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustment additions: non-deductible expenses, depreciation/finance lease adjustments, TP true-ups and GAAR modifications.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include excess interest above thin cap, non-deductible management fees, overstated related-party royalties, entertainment expense over-limits, advertisement costs not actually incurred, and any transfer pricing adjustment proposed by STA. Non-resident related party transactions not reported on Schedule A105000 may trigger the mandatory filing amendment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustment reductions: tax-exempt income, qualified dividends, government-grant deductions, R&D super deduction, and foreign tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim the 100% R&D super deduction only for qualifying ad-tech algorithm R&D performed in China. Foreign income tax paid in Hong Kong can be credited under the DTA if the WFOE has foreign-source income, but not against WHT on Chinese-source dividends; attach Schedule A108000 and DTA forms.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before loss offset: total profit adjusted by additions and reductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If this line is positive after adding TP recharacterisation of HK royalty/service payments, use it as the starting point for applying carried-over losses. Any offset of a HK/offshore loss is prohibited unless the loss is from a Chinese resident branch and complies with loss linkage rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward offset available in the current year from prior years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PRC general losses have a 5-year carryforward; 10 years for qualifying HNTE. Losses cannot be deducted if the loss period under a HK group relief concept is claimed elsewhere; cross-border loss pooling with HK parent is not available.

This is the income base for computing annual CIT. If revenue has been under-declared due to related-party re-invoicing, the competent tax bureau will reconstruct this line using deemed-PE or arm's length method.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax rate, tax reduction, tax exemption and final CIT payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 25% headline rate; 15% if HNTE; 5% effective rate for qualified small low-profit enterprises. Deduct quarterly prepayments already made. Any balance payable must be settled by 31 May; unpaid amount accrues 0.05% daily surcharge and may trigger an exit ban for responsible directors.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late annual/quarterly filing under the Tax Administration and Collection Law (TACL) may attract a warning and fine up to RMB 2,000, rising to RMB 2,000-RMB 10,000 for repeated/serious late filing; unpaid tax carries a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05%. Under TACL Art. 63, underpaying CIT through false or fictitious invoices, undisclosed related-party income, or sham contracts is punished by recovery of the underpaid tax plus a civil penalty from 50% to 500% of the underpaid amount. Withholding agents that fail to withhold on outbound dividends/interest/royalties may be held jointly liable and fined 50%-300% of the amount required to be withheld. Tax evasion above the criminal thresholds triggers Criminal Law Art. 201: imprisonment up to 7 years plus criminal fines, confiscation, and travel/exit restrictions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory dividend withholding tax under PRC EIT Law Articles 3 and 37; reduced to 5% under the Mainland/HK Double Taxation Arrangement if the HK beneficial owner is a company holding at least 25% of the WFOE's shares throughout the 365 days preceding the dividend distribution and has substantive business in Hong Kong.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before paying an outbound dividend, the HK shareholder must obtain a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Inland Revenue Department for the relevant year and submit to the WFOE withholding agent: (1) the TRC; (2) a beneficial ownership declaration; (3) shareholding register and 365-day holding proof; (4) Hong Kong economic substance/CIGA documentation (office, staff, board minutes, income tax returns, bank accounts and decision-making for the ad-tech investment); (5) the dividend resolution and (6) an undertaking not to conduit the dividend to a non-HK resident. The WFOE files the withholding return on the e-tax portal, applies for the 5% treaty rate, and withholds at the 5% rate only after STA acceptance; if the application is rejected, 10% must be withheld and a tax treaty MAP/refund claim may be pursued.
